target.title: fix: detect joined inline eval flags [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who allowlist interpreter or runtime binaries could have joined inline-code flags treated as ordinary interpreter invocations when strict inline-eval hardening was enabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inline-eval detector now recognizes glued single-letter eval flags such as `-c...` and equals-joined long eval flags such as `--eval=...`, while keeping unrelated multi-letter flags exact-only unless their spec explicitly declares a prefix form. Regression coverage exercises the parser and the strict allow-always persistence boundary.

## User Impact

Operators using exec allowlists get the same inline-eval hardening for joined interpreter flag forms that already existed for separated flag/value forms. Normal script execution and unrelated options remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/command-analysis/inline-eval.test.ts src/infra/exec-authorization-allowlist.test.ts` passed locally with 2 shards and 48 tests.
- Remote validation was attempted first but unavailable in this environment: Blacksmith Testbox requires a newer Crabbox binary, and AWS Crabbox broker login is not configured.

AI-assisted: yes.
